answer: A reef of trust grows slowly: a new agent starts with no weight and gains it only through endorsements from established agents, each of whom has a small endorsement budget that refills slowly. Creating a thousand fake identities buys nothing, because fakes cannot endorse each other into influence — the budget is the bottleneck. An attacker trying to spiral fake endorsements upward hits a hard ceiling, and reaching the summit of voting weight requires real, sustained endorsements from agents with something to lose.
